claims.statement: A realization ladder shall distinguish an articulated idea, a consistent software model, an executable virtual witness, a device deployment, a qualified observation system, a physical finding, a causally attributed effect and an authorized external effect.
claims.boundary: Methodological separation for this addendum; it does not assert that every project must use the same labels.

claims.statement: The existence or execution of a software model does not by itself establish the physical phenomenon represented by that model.
claims.boundary: Scientific inference boundary; a physical conclusion requires separately stated bridge premises and evidence.

claims.statement: Within this addendum a system qualifies as an observation system only when acquisition, calibration, temporal binding, source provenance, integrity, falsifiability and governance are all satisfied in the declared scope.
claims.boundary: Operational predicate OBS(X) for the addendum; no particular game or deployed system is certified by this definition alone.

claims.statement: Imagination can be treated as a generator of counterfactual implementation candidates, but an imagined candidate is not thereby an observation or a verified fact.
claims.boundary: Author-inspired methodological interpretation; it is not a neuroscientific theory of imagination or consciousness.

claims.statement: An undisclosed epistemic advantage shall not substitute for provenance, truth status, contestability or authorization of an irreversible effect.
claims.boundary: Epistemic-fairness guardrail for observation and effect systems; it does not require equal knowledge among all participants.

claims.statement: The author-originated thesis that comparable observation or information systems already operate without official public knowledge remains empirically unresolved.
claims.boundary: No named deployment, independently inspectable artifact, measurement record or replication is established by this addendum.

claims.statement: The finite deterministic replay model neither proves superdeterminism nor disproves any specified account of free will.
claims.boundary: Explicit non-claim boundary; no complete ontology of the universe or human decision-making is supplied.

claims.statement: Physical future-to-past information transfer remains unestablished by the virtual-time witness and by this audio-derived addendum.
claims.boundary: A physical bridge hypothesis, calibrated experiment, controls and falsification criterion are still required.
